components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      x-class-extra-annotation: |-
        @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.PostcodeValidation
        @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.AddressFormValidation
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            The pet owner's optional honorific title, one of MR, MRS, MS or DR.
            When present it is combined with the lastName to form the read-only
            salutation ('<title> <lastName>'); when absent the salutation is
            just the lastName.
          type: string
          example: 'DR'
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The flat postal address of the pet owner, accepted for backward
            compatibility. The value is normalized before it is stored and
            returned: surrounding whitespace is trimmed and internal runs of
            whitespace collapsed to a single space, it is upper-cased, and common
            street-type abbreviations are expanded as whole words (ST->STREET,
            RD->ROAD, AVE->AVENUE), e.g. '  12  main st ' is stored as '12 MAIN
            STREET'. Optional: an owner is accepted when it supplies an address in
            EITHER the flat form here OR a non-blank structured 'addressLine1'. On
            the response this holds the composed address: the normalized
            'addressLine1' (with a single space and the normalized 'addressLine2'
            appended when present) when structured fields were supplied, otherwise
            the normalized flat address. When supplied directly it must not be
            blank after normalization.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.AddressValidation"
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address. Preferred
            over the flat 'address' when present. Normalized with the same rules as
            'address' (trimmed, whitespace-collapsed, upper-cased, street-type
            abbreviations expanded). An owner is accepted when it supplies a
            non-blank 'addressLine1' or a flat 'address', plus a city.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '10 King St'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal address.
            Normalized with the same rules as 'addressLine1'. When present it is
            appended to the normalized 'addressLine1', separated by a single space,
            to form the composed 'address' returned on the response.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Unit 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. The value is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; an explicit
            leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise country code '+61'
            is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national
            digits. The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+' and is
            stored and returned in that canonical form (e.g. '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '0412 345 678'
          x-field-extra-annotation: |-
            @jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank
            @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.TelephoneValidation
        email:
          title: Email
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional, but when present it
            must be a syntactically valid address; the value is stored and
            returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
          x-field-extra-annotation: |-
            @jakarta.validation.constraints.Email
            @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.EmailDomainValidation
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; validated only when present,
            so an owner created without a postcode stays valid. When present it
            must be valid for the owner's city: for a city with a known region
            (Sydney->NSW 2000-2099, Melbourne->VIC 3000-3099, Brisbane->QLD
            4000-4099) the postcode must fall in that region's inclusive range; a
            city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and
            returned exactly as given.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date. A date later than the server's current date is rejected.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.PastOrPresent"
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The pet owner's date of birth, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Optional.
            When present it is used to derive the owner's read-only ageBand,
            computed against the owner's registrationDate.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone

      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object

The implementation is complete and the full test suite is green.

## Summary

I implemented the `ownerSegment` field on the Owner API response, following the existing Spring/MapStruct/OpenAPI conventions in the codebase.

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added a read-only `ownerSegment` string property (with the enum of the four allowed values) to the Owner schema, mirroring how sibling derived fields like `locality` and `ageBand` are declared. This drives code generation of `OwnerDto.OwnerSegmentEnum`.

2. **`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — Added a `@Mapping(target = "ownerSegment", ...)` entry plus a `toOwnerSegment(Owner)` default method that:
   - picks `PREMIUM` when `owner.getMembershipLevel() >= 3`, else `STANDARD`;
   - picks `METRO` when the derived `locality` (reused via the existing `toLocality`) is `NSW`, `VIC`, or `QLD`, else `REGIONAL`;
   - joins them as `<TIER>_<AREA>`.

Reusing the existing `getMembershipLevel()` and `toLocality()` logic keeps the segment consistent with the already-reported `membershipLevel` and `locality` fields.

**Tests:** Both acceptance tests pass — `STANDARD_METRO` for a known region (Sydney→NSW, level 2) and `STANDARD_REGIONAL` for an unknown city — and the full suite reports `BUILD SUCCESS`.

Note: this isn't a git repository, so I made no commit.
